coverage_notes:
DETECTION / ASCERTAINMENT (dominant limitation for any tissue-sequenced cohort). Every claim of a large ESR1-mutant effect size in this graph derives from ctDNA-genotyped populations (SoFEA, EFECT, PALOMA-3, BOLERO-2, PADA-1, EMERALD, SERENA-6, EMBER-3, GuardantINFORM). Tissue-only ascertainment gives systematically lower prevalence: 0.16% in treatment-naive primary tumors (C-027), 0% in 32 biopsies after adjuvant-AI progression (C-007), 0/23 in neoadjuvant-AI-resistant primaries (C-028), versus 25-40% in post-AI metastatic plasma. Any tissue-based ESR1-mutant group is therefore expected to be a small, biased subset enriched for late metastatic re-biopsy.

No study found that quantifies ESR1 mutation sensitivity of MSK-IMPACT specifically, or reports MSK-IMPACT ESR1 call rates stratified by specimen type (primary versus metastatic biopsy) and by timing relative to aromatase inhibitor exposure. The nearest available evidence is a 43-patient ddPCR tissue-versus-plasma concordance study (C-029) and a Tempus xT/xF real-world comparison (C-025).

No study found reporting the fraction of ESR1 mutations that fall below the limit of detection of standard FFPE bulk tumor sequencing because of subclonality. Spoerke 2016 reports low ESR1 allele fractions relative to PIK3CA in ctDNA, but the numeric variant-allele-frequency comparison could not be verified verbatim from the retrieved abstract and is therefore not asserted as a claim.

POPULATION GAPS. No claim found linking somatic ESR1 mutation frequency or effect size to genetic ancestry. Searches for ancestry-stratified somatic ESR1 data returned only germline ESR1 polymorphism/pharmacogenetics work and general ancestry-related differences in TP53/PIK3CA. No cohort with reported non-European ancestry breakdown for ESR1-mutant outcomes was found.

No claim found stratified by menopausal status. All major ctDNA trial analyses retrieved (BOLERO-2, SoFEA, EFECT) are postmenopausal by design; premenopausal patients on ovarian suppression plus AI are effectively unstudied for ESR1 emergence.

De novo versus recurrent metastatic disease: only indirect evidence found. Web summaries assert lower ESR1 prevalence in de novo metastatic presentation, but the primary npj Breast Cancer 2018 abstract states no association with primary-tumor pathology or time to distant recurrence (C-031), and I could not verify a de-novo-versus-recurrent effect size verbatim in any primary record. This is a genuine open gap.

No claim found on ESR1 mutation frequency or effect modification by histology (invasive lobular versus ductal). Targeted Europe PMC searching for ESR1 and lobular returned no primary quantitative report.

No claim found on ESR1 mutation and outcome stratified by age at metastatic diagnosis, race/ethnicity as recorded in health records, or geography outside North America and Western Europe.

TEMPORAL STALENESS. The foundational discovery cohorts are small and old: Toy 2013 (14/80 tumors), Robinson 2013 (11 patients), Jeselsohn 2014 (76 metastatic ER+ samples). The largest tissue-based prevalence estimate found remains a pooled cBioPortal reanalysis from 2022 (C-027). No tissue-sequenced cohort with n > 1000 published after 2022 reporting ESR1-mutant clinical outcomes was found.

CONTRADICTIONS LEFT UNRESOLVED (deliberately not reconciled). (1) Toy 2013 reports mutants reduce antagonist efficacy, Robinson 2013 reports continued anti-estrogen responsiveness in vitro (C-001 vs C-002). (2) Fulvestrant differential benefit in ESR1-mutant disease (C-011, C-016) versus Spoerke 2016 finding no association with fulvestrant resistance and no PFS difference (C-017), and Clatot 2016 finding ESR1 prognostic but not predictive of subsequent therapy choice (C-021). (3) PALOMA-3 shows undiminished palbociclib benefit in ESR1-mutant patients (C-009, C-010) while MCF7 knock-in and xenograft models show frank palbociclib resistance (C-026). (4) ESR1 mutations enriched after CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure in a 3958-patient real-world dataset (C-025) versus lower prevalence after CDK4/6 inhibitor in the 2018 cfDNA cohort (C-032). (5) Uniform 'fulvestrant retains activity' framing versus variant-specific plasmaMATCH data where Y537S does poorly and Y537C does well (C-024).

INTERPRETATION HAZARD for downstream stages: ESR1 mutation is tightly confounded with duration and setting of prior aromatase inhibitor exposure (C-003, C-006, C-033) and with metastatic disease burden/aggressiveness (C-020, C-022). Several sources argue the mutation may mark prior endocrine exposure and worse disease rather than acting as a specific AI-resistance switch; this alternative remains live and is not adjudicated here.

NOT FOUND: any randomized comparison of aromatase inhibitor versus fulvestrant restricted to tissue-detected (rather than plasma-detected) ESR1 mutations. The INTERACT study protocol (NCT number visible only in a ClinicalTrials.gov PDF, not independently verified here) appeared in search results but no results publication was retrieved.

NOT FOUND: verbatim-verifiable ESR1-specific subgroup results from MONALEESA-2/-3/-7 or MONARCH-2/-3 ctDNA analyses. The pooled MONALEESA ctDNA paper (Ann Oncol 2023, PMID 37673211) abstract lists ERBB2, FAT3, FRS2, MDM2, SFRP1, ZNF217 as benefit-associated and ANO1, CDKN2A/2B/2C, RB1 as resistance-associated but does not state an ESR1 result in the retrieved abstract, so no MONALEESA ESR1 claim is asserted.

PREPRINT COVERAGE is thin: one relevant 2025 bioRxiv preprint was located (C-040) and could not be quoted verbatim from the retrieved rendering, so it is recorded unverified at low confidence. No medRxiv clinical preprint specific to ESR1-mutant outcomes was located.

SCHEMA CAVEAT: this file was authored without read access to pipeline/schemas/claim_graph.schema.json (the literature-mapper toolset has no read tool and file:// fetches are rejected). Field names and nesting follow the specification given in the task brief. Values chosen for enum-typed fields are: predicate.effect from the stated enum; direction_certainty restricted to reported_significant and trend_only; confidence in high/moderate/low; context.model_system in human/cell_line/xenograft/in_silico; evidence.design in randomized_trial/rct_secondary_analysis/prospective_cohort/retrospective_cohort/preclinical/preprint/review. If validate.py rejects any of these, the fix is a value or key rename, not a content change.
